title: From text to design: a framework to leverage LLM agents for automated CAD generation

live_model.evidence: "ChatGPT-4 Turbo was selected as it was the most advanced and stable multimodal LLM available at the time of the experiments."; Table 2 row "GPT-4 Turbo 13/15 (87%) 4/15 (27%) 6/15 (40%) 3/15 (20%) 26/60 (43%)" (stepPlanning agent workflow).

prompt.location: Appendix A ("Each geometry creation was called with three distinct textual prompts, see Appendix A"); Fig. 1 framework flowchart
prompt.note: Any LLM supporting API-based interaction can be integrated (line ~300); function-call file and predefined context also referenced in Fig. 1.

claim.metric: success rate (%), GPT-4 Turbo, stepPlanning agent workflow, Total across 4 test geometries
claim.location: Table 2 (Success rates of LLMs across test geometries using the stepPlanning agent workflow), row 'GPT-4 Turbo', Total column: 26/60 (43%)

data.source: 4 predefined test geometries (box, corner plate, u-profile, toy car) with 3 textual prompts each and ground-truth CAD models (Fig. 2, Appendix A); FCRC bracket case study is a cited published benchmark (Schmidt 2016)

notes: API-based, function-calling agent workflow; GPT-4 Turbo is one of five LLMs compared (Mistral Large, GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4 Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, GPT-4o) under the stepPlanning workflow, with 15 attempts x 4 geometries = 60 total. GPT-4 Turbo also has separate Table 1 (chatGPT-4 Turbo across all 4 agent workflows, 111/240) and Table 3/4 (FCRC bracket case study) results if a different cell is preferred.
